chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever grows hair, let him take good care of it or trim it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on growing and maintaining hair?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the principle of *ihsan* (excellence) in personal appearance, linking grooming to spiritual discipline. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition), where neglecting one's appearance is seen as a form of spiritual or social disarray, while well-kept hair signifies respect for oneself and others.
